Estimate the delay distribution of a reporting triangle

Source: R/delay_completeness.R
delay_distribution_v1.Rd

Estimates the probability that a case is reported on each delay day, from 0 to max_delay_days - 1. The estimate uses every reference week, and corrects for the weeks that are not fully reported yet.

Usage

delay_distribution_v1(x, max_delay_days)

Arguments

x

A csfmt_reporting_triangle_v3 with one series. With more than one time_series_id, the function stops with an error that names the id columns of x.

max_delay_days

The delay horizon in days, delay day 0 to max_delay_days - 1.

Value

A data.table with one row per delay day and four columns:

  • delay: the delay day, an integer from 0 to max_delay_days - 1.

  • day_after: the integer delay - 6. Day 1 is the Monday after the reference week.

  • week_after: the integer delay / 7 where delay is a multiple of 7, and NA on every other day.

  • p: the probability of a report on delay day delay. With max_delay_days = 1, p is 1.

Details

The function uses the rows of reporting_triangle_matrix() whose reference Monday is on or before the as-of date, attr(x, "as_of"). age_days is the number of days from that Monday to the as-of date. A row has seen delay days 0 to n_seen - 1, with n_seen = pmin(age_days + 1, max_delay_days).

The product-limit estimate starts at the last delay day, where the cumulative distribution F is 1. Then F(d - 1) / F(d) is the count reported by delay d - 1, divided by the count reported by delay d. Both sums use only the rows that have seen delay d. Where the count by delay d is 0, F(d - 1) = F(d). A report at delay max_delay_days or later is not in the estimate, so p is conditional on a report within the horizon.

The function does not choose a window of weeks. It also keeps the weeks with a reporting outage, which outage_weeks_v1() finds. To leave weeks out, filter x before the call. A triangle filtered with [ keeps its as-of date.

Delay convention

Delay day 0 is the Monday of the reference ISO week, and delay d is d days after it. NorSySS readers count from the end of the week instead. The columns day_after and week_after give their count.

  • day_after k is the k-th day after the week, so day 1 is the Monday after the week. The values from -6 to 0 are days inside the week: -6 is its Monday, and 0 is the Sunday that ends it.

  • week_after k is the Monday k weeks after the week, so week 1 is day 1 and week 2 is day 8.

For example, week 2026-46 starts on Monday 2026-11-09. Delay 7 is Monday 2026-11-16, which is day 1 and week 1. Delay 14 is day 8 and week 2. A horizon of 63 days, 9 weeks, puts week 8 at delay 56, inside the horizon.

See also

reporting_completion_v1(), which pools only the weeks old enough to be fully reported.

Examples

monday <- as.Date("2023-01-02") + 7 * rep(0:39, each = 3)
set.seed(1)
d <- data.table::data.table(
  isoyearweek_reference = format(monday, "%G-%V"),
  reporting_date = monday + rep(c(3, 10, 17), 40),
  numerator = rpois(120, c(30, 15, 5)),
  indicator_tag = "x", location_code = "nation", age = "total", sex = "total"
)
d <- d[reporting_date <= as.Date("2023-01-02") + 7 * 39 + 6]
tri <- csfmt_reporting_triangle_v3(
  d,
  id_cols = c("indicator_tag", "location_code", "age", "sex")
)

# this series reports on days 3, 10 and 17 after the reference Monday
dd <- delay_distribution_v1(tri, max_delay_days = 21)
dd[p > 0]
#>    delay day_after week_after         p
#>    <int>     <int>      <int>     <num>
#> 1:     3        -3         NA 0.5850863
#> 2:    10         4         NA 0.3143283
#> 3:    17        11         NA 0.1005854

# the last 20 reference weeks only
delay_distribution_v1(tri[isoyearweek_reference >= "2023-21"], 21)[p > 0]
#>    delay day_after week_after         p
#>    <int>     <int>      <int>     <num>
#> 1:     3        -3         NA 0.5773124
#> 2:    10         4         NA 0.3210895
#> 3:    17        11         NA 0.1015982
